/record/physicalDescription	Canopied bed. Huali wood, with woven matting seat. China; 1600-1700. A six-post canopied bed, of dark reddish-brown huali wood, which can be dismantled into seventeen sections, viz; base platform, 4 x corner posts, 2 x front lower balustrade, 2 x side lower balustrade, 1 x back lower balustrade, 1 x front upper balustrade, 2 x side upper balustrade, 1 x back upper balustrade, roof. The top has a frame of huali wood, with three-piece butt-joined floating panels of an unidentified softwood, probably coniferous. All components parts are of circular section, without moulding. The pattern of the openwork balustrading is two rows of plain double verticals at the top. The tenons on the corner posts are quater-circular cross-section. The tenons fixing the lower balustrade to the vertical posts are simple rectangles, but those fixing the upper balustrade are the slide-locking type. Double tenons are exposed on the short sides of the base frame, and single tenons on the sides of the top frame.
